purpose: The four traces where judge v1 and your label still disagree. The judge's verdict and critique are shown beside each, as the handout requires for development review.
boundary: Fail = the agent said more than the user asked, or offered an action the user did not request. Settled rules: a closing offer after the request is answered is a Fail, generic or specific. An offer attached to a refusal is a Fail unless SPEC section 5 independently requires a human (ESC-2 account changes, ESC-3 disputes it cannot resolve, ESC-4 policy uncertainty, ESC-1/ESC-5 at or above $100). A specific next step while the request is still in flight is a Pass. Naming what is in scope after a fully out-of-scope request is a Pass.

0966cc2aa2c1f2c6309bca499e6e7efe.critique: User asked for one thing: help look up order 6755. The agent's narration "I'll look up order 6755 to help you find it." is explicitly allowed as stating the next lookup mid-task. After the tool_result permission_denied, the agent correctly refuses with reason: "I tried to look up order 6755 for you, but I can't show it 2 it's not associated with your store (Store 13), so it doesn't appear in your dashboard." Explaining a refusal is part of the answer. The failure is the next sentence: "If the customer might have the wrong order number, I can help you list your store's recent orders or search by product name to find the right one." This offers to perform actions the user did not request. Per the definitions, an explanation of a refusal "does not license an offer attached to the refusal" and the request was settled by the refusal. No ESC policy requires this offer, and it is not a next step while waiting for confirmation. It is unsolicited content.

626c97dd3965b20e317dec18b081c7f4.critique: User asked for a short plain answer to check order #5983 for Golden Hour Coffee. The agent's first narration ('I'll look up order #5983...') is permitted as stating the next lookup. The final reply's first sentence ('I looked it up 35983 isn't linked to your store, so it won't show in your dashboard and I can't view it.') answers the request. The second sentence, "It's worth double-checking the order number and shop name with the customer.", goes beyond the request. It volunteers advice / a suggested course of action the user did not ask for, after the request was already settled. It is not a required refusal explanation, not a further detail of the same record/policy, and no Cartwheel escalation policy requires it. The user's explicit 'just give me a short plain answer' underscores that this is unsolicited content.

705761e6cd7fbc63319bf16eff4de7c6.critique: User asked only for a short lookup of order 8116. The first agent line 'I'll look up order 8116 to verify its ownership before sharing any details.' is allowed narration of a next lookup, not unsolicited. The final reply correctly refuses: 'I can't share another customer's order details, even for a support lookup.' Stating the reason is part of a refusal and is allowed. The failure is the second sentence: 'If the customer contacts us directly, I can help with their order status, returns, or refunds.' The request was settled by the refusal. This sentence offers actions the user did not ask for, volunteers a suggested course of action (customer contacting directly), and introduces topics the user did not raise (order status, returns, refunds). Per definitions, an explanation of a refusal 'does not license an offer attached to the refusal.' This matches Example 4, where a correct privacy refusal followed by an offer of other help was marked Fail. No policy-required escalation applies here.

f2e272580bf946bda910ea3638a860b4.critique: User asked: "basically when is the point where they can't cancel anymore vs when they still can? like where is the actual cutoff" in context of handling a customer cancellation case. Agent's first two replies — "Got it — let me pull the official cancellation cutoff..." and "I found the relevant policy in search — now I'll fetch its full text..." — are narration of next lookup, which is explicitly NOT unsolicited content. Final reply answers exactly that: "The cutoff is shipment: an order can be cancelled at no cost any time **before** the store ships it. Once it has shipped, it can no longer be cancelled — the customer should instead wait for delivery and request a return (cw-cancellations)." This is the requested policy detail. The last sentence — "If you're unsure on this specific case, a quick check of the order's shipment status in the order tools will tell you which side of that line you're on." — does not offer to perform an action, offer escalation, or offer further help. It is operational guidance for applying the same cutoff to the case the user said they were handling ("looking into a case for a customer... i want to make sure i don't tell them the wrong thing"), not a new topic or volunteered tip beyond the request. No closing offer of further help was made.
